kioskAccess.scanTitle: Scan with your tablet or phone
kioskAccess.howTitle: How to set up your kiosk
kioskAccess.howSubtitle: Four steps, from any Android tablet, iPad, or phone.
steps: Open the address above in your tablet or phone browser (Chrome or Safari) — or scan the QR code.
Add the page to your home screen so it opens like an app.
Put it in full screen. On iPad/iPhone use "Guided Access"; on Android use screen pinning to lock it on the kiosk.
Place the tablet or phone on your counter. Paid orders go straight to your kitchen display.
kioskAccess.tip: Tip: any tablet or Android/iPhone with a browser works. No special hardware to buy.
kioskAccess.noHardwareTitle: One-person taco shop? You don't even need a kiosk
kioskAccess.noHardwareBody: With QR Menu, customers order and pay from their own phone by scanning a code at the counter — zero hardware to buy or set up.

whatsappOps.title: Inventory and expenses over WhatsApp
whatsappOps.subtitle: Send a photo or a voice note. It becomes a purchase, a count, or waste.

status.title: The number your team messages
status.noNumberYet: No number is connected for your restaurant yet.
status.notConnectedBody: Get in touch to connect your business WhatsApp. The number keeps working normally on the phone: customers still message you and a person still answers them. All this adds is your team being able to send photos and voice notes into inventory.
status.platformNote: You're on the Desktop Kitchen number. It works the same, but connecting your own business WhatsApp is better — your team messages the number they already know.
status.save: Save this number on your team's phones.

who.title: Who can use it
who.body: Only employees with a phone on file. The system recognizes who sent the message by their number — if yours isn't on the list, it won't answer you.
who.empty: No employee has a phone registered yet. Add at least one to get started.
who.missing: {{count}} active employee(s) without a phone on file.
who.customersNote: Customers who message this number get NO automated reply. The bot only answers your team; customers are still handled by a person on the phone.

receipt.title: Photo of a receipt, delivery note, or slip
receipt.body: Handwritten sales note, supplier delivery note, supermarket receipt, or the little slip from the card terminal. It pulls vendor, items, quantities, and costs: stock goes into inventory and the expense is recorded with the photo attached.

count.title: Photo of the fridge, freezer, or shelf
count.body: Counts the visible units per brand and compares them against what the system says. A variance over 10% raises a shrinkage alert. It's honest about what it can't see: if rows are hidden behind, it says so and lowers its confidence.

voice.title: Voice note
voice.body: "I threw out three carne asada burritos" records the waste. It also handles counts and turning menu items on or off when something runs out.

how.title: How it works, step by step
how.subtitle: Same for every case. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
steps: Save the number above on the employee's phone, like any other contact.
Send the photo or voice note over WhatsApp. You can add a caption to steer it: "count", or the supplier's name.
Within seconds you get a draft of what it understood: items, quantities, and costs, line by line.
Check it and reply SI to save, or NO to discard. If it found items that aren't in your inventory, reply AGREGAR and it creates them first.
You have 60 minutes to reply. After that the draft expires on its own and nothing is saved.

tips.title: Getting it right the first time
items: Fit the whole receipt in frame, with good light and no folds.
For counts, one photo per section: a single shelf or tray per message, not the whole fridge from across the room.
On handwritten notes, what matters is each line's total — not the price per kilo. The system works out the unit cost itself.
It works over WhatsApp, not SMS: plain text messages don't carry photos in Mexico.
If it doesn't recognize an item it leaves it unlinked and tells you. Reply AGREGAR to create it.

whatsappOps.privacy: Photos are stored alongside the expense so you can look them up later. Only your restaurant can see them.
